articles.title: Rams RB Blake Corum pulls off ultra-rare feat vs. Packers last done in 2002
articles.summary: Packers last done in 2002 appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here. The Los Angeles Rams turned to Blake Corum in gashing the Green Bay Packers. Corum’s late one-yard touchdown did more than extend his scoring streak, though.
body: Corum scored on his 26th birthday, joining the revered legend Bruce in this category per ESPN Insights.
“Blake Corum is the first Rams player to score a TD on their birthday since Isaac Bruce in 2002,” the account posted on the social media website X, formerly Twitter.

The Pro Football Hall of Famer Bruce scored his birthday touchdown as a 30-year-old. Rams fans remember Bruce for helping create the “Greatest Show on Turf” days during the St. Louis years. Which features two Super Bowl appearances including the 1999 season title alongside quarterback Kurt Warner, running back Marshall Faulk and fellow wide receiver Torry Holt.

Corum hit one more career milestone too. He put together back-to-back 100-yard games for the first time in his young career. Corum briefly delivered 100 yards in the rout of the Arizona Cardinals on Nov. 15. But he wore down the Packers with an astonishing 184 yards on 32 carries against the NFC North foe.

articles.title: Stipe Miocic Opens Door to UFC Return at 44 but Has One Major Demand
articles.summary: Stipe Miocic is widely regarded as the greatest heavyweight in UFC history. The former two-time champion holds several divisional records, including the most consecutive title defenses (3), total title defenses (4), and fight-night bonuses (9).
body: With a professional record of 20-5, the Croatian-American retired following his loss to Jon Jones at UFC 309 at Madison Square Garden. Although he was already 42 at the time, Miocic has not completely ruled out a return to the Octagon. However, the former champion has made it clear that any comeback would need to come with a significant financial incentive.

In a recent interview with Casino.org, Miocic opened up about the possibility of ending his retirement and said, “A lot of money. I guess there’s always a chance of coming out of retirement. Never say never. I’d probably fight anyone. I’ve never really cared about who I fought, so there’s no dream fight. But if there’s a lot of money involved, then I would definitely do it.”

Miocic boasts one of the most impressive resumes in heavyweight history, having shared the Octagon with the likes of Daniel Cormier, Jon Jones, Francis Ngannou, Alistair Overeem, and Junior dos Santos. Having faced and defeated several generations of heavyweight contenders, the former champion has accomplished virtually everything possible in the sport.

articles.title: England's All Blacks Tests 'World Cup practice' | 'Ireland still not contenders'
articles.summary: Head coaches Steve Borthwick of England, Andy Farrell of Ireland and Dave Rennie of New Zealand speak to media ahead of the final weekend of the inaugural Nations Championship.
body: England, having come into the tournament under a cloud of pressure following the worst Six Nations display in their history earlier this year (four losses, fifth place), have stormed to victories over Australia, Japan and New Zealand this month.

Last week, Borthwick's side secured a record 25-point victory over the All Blacks at Allianz Stadium. With England finishing second behind France in the northern hemisphere standings and New Zealand runners-up to South Africa in the southern hemisphere table, the two sides are now set for an immediate rematch.
England face the All Blacks again at Twickenham on Saturday, with Borthwick viewing the latest clash as valuable preparation for the Rugby World Cup in Australia in 10 months' time.
"The nature of this tournament, it's a new tournament, is the understanding that international games have that level of jeopardy," Borthwick told the media on Wednesday.

articles.title: 'All coming together' - Isak repaying Liverpool faith
articles.summary: Alexander Isak's two goals against Club Brugge take his tally for the season to 10 as the striker continues to show why Liverpool last year paid £125m to bring him to the club.
body: Liverpool fans have needed to be patient to see the best of Alexander Isak after an injury-hit start to his career, but the striker is now proving the wait has been worth it.
By scoring twice against Club Brugge in the Champions League, Isak took his tally for the season to 10 - more than double his total for his first season at the Reds.
Of course, that campaign was disrupted; he had no pre-season because of his protracted £125m move from Newcastle and then suffered a broken leg in December.
But Isak is now in a hot streak of form, having scored four goals in his past four games for Liverpool.

articles.summary: Jamie Carragher says Manchester United goalkeeper Senne Lammens' confidence is a cause for concern after his howler cost Mauricio Pochettino a first win since taking charge.
body: It was a nightmare performance for Lammens, who unnecessarily gave away the penalty for Luis Suarez's opener just 75 seconds after saving the Sporting striker's poorly taken first spot-kick.

Lammens, 24, then spilled a routine cross late in the second half which allowed Suarez to equalise for 2-2, denying United a first away win of the season and first away Champions League win for five years.

The Belgium international, signed from Club Brugge last summer, restored calm between the sticks last season after Andre Onana's calamitous spell as No 1, but has had a poor start to his second season at Old Trafford.
Delivering his verdict on Lammens' performance, Carragher said on CBS: "You worry about the confidence of that goalkeeper now.

articles.title: Poch denied first Man Utd win by Lammens howler at Sporting
articles.summary: Mauricio Pochettino was denied a first victory as Manchester United head coach by a goalkeeping howler from Senne Lammens in an incident-packed 2-2 draw with Sporting in the Champions League as Youri Tielemans was sent off late on.
body: United looked to be on course for a first away win of the season after captain Bruno Fernandes scored two goals in the first five minutes of the second half only for Lammens to spill the ball in the box for Luis Suarez to equalise with his second goal of the game.

Pochettino thought United had gone back in front for a second time shortly after Lammens' error when Sporting goalkeeper Kaique punched into his own net at a corner. However, it was ruled out following an on-field review for a foul by substitute Patrick Dorgu.

It was a damaging night for Lammens, who gave away the penalty for Suarez's first goal just 75 seconds after saving the Sporting striker's poorly taken spot-kick. The man brought into replace the error-prone Andre Onana is now beginning to resemble his predecessor.

Fernandes' equaliser three minutes after the restart came from the third penalty of what was a bizarre match. Few moments topped the United skipper's freakish second goal which came thanks a tame effort bouncing up off a divot in the ground and into back of the net.

articles.title: Isak and Wirtz power Liverpool to easy victory at Club Brugge
articles.summary: Liverpool recovered from their shock defeat to Fenerbahce in their last Champions League outing to beat Club Brugge 3-0 and improve their chances of a top-eight league phase finish.
body: Andoni Iraola's side have had no problem scoring goals in Europe, but faced issues keeping them out. Brugge were most obliging hosts in that respect, a far cry from the regularly free-scoring side that have so far averaged 2.75 goals per game and beaten Inter Milan at the San Siro.

Felix Lemarechal was the home side's greatest threat. But Alexander Isak was far more decisive, netting the opener following Yann Sommer's misplaced pass before rounding off the scoring in the second half with a deft chip to beat the goalkeeper. Sandwiched between was a superb strike from the in-form Florian Wirtz, set up by a surging run from Rio Ngumoha.

Brugge got better, Lemarechal twice forced Alisson into saves and Nicolo Tresoldi, who has scored the same number of Champions League goals as Erling Haaland this term, also called the Brazilian into action. But Liverpool were creatively superior. Momentum is building.

articles.title: Packers' Christian Watson Leaves vs. Rams After Taking Hard Hit; S Kam Kinchens Ejected
articles.summary: Green Bay Packers wide receiver Christian Watson was on the wrong end of a hit that led to an ejection in Wednesday's game against the Los Angeles Rams. Watson took a hard hit up high from Rams safety Kam Kinchens as he tried to make a sideline grab late in the first half.
body: Kinchens, meanwhile, was penalized for unnecessary roughness and was ejected for his hit on Watson. It didn't appear that Kinchens made helmet-to-helmet contact with Watson on the play, leading many to question the call on social media.

The penalty was also pretty significant. The Packers were facing a fourth-and-1 on the play when Kinchens was ejected, and his hit was hard enough that it caused Watson to drop the ball. But with the penalty, the Packers got a fourth-down redo as Green Bay wide receiver Matthew Golden was penalized for offensive pass interference on the play.
Green Bay opted to kick a field goal after the offsetting penalties, allowing it to tie the game, 13-13.
Just as he has all season, Watson made a big impact in the first half of Wednesday's game. He had a game-high four receptions for 65 yards and a touchdown through the game's first 30 minutes.

articles.title: Sammy’s Sportsbook Whispers: Big Ten's CFP Hopes Dwindle With QB Injuries
articles.summary: Is the Big Ten only getting one team into the College Football Playoff? A quick check of the market shows that only Oregon is favored to make it into this year’s 12-team field.
body: "Think of all the Big Ten quarterbacks that got hurt," professional bettor Slice told me over the phone. "Dante Moore, Josh Hoover, Julian Sayin, then Nico [Iamaleava] and [Ty] Dieffenbach on the same UCLA team. Those four teams could’ve all made the dance with better quarterback health."

UCLA (10-1) would undoubtedly punch its ticket with a victory over USC this Saturday, but the Bruins are 7-point underdogs with third-stringer Madden Iamaleava expected to get the start at the Rose Bowl.

"They adjusted it 10 points," former Vegas bookmaker Ed Salmons said. "It seems like an over move, but the third-string kid for UCLA froze like a deer in headlights against Michigan. He had a wide-open field in front of him and could’ve run for days but threw the ball into coverage. He’s not functional."
It’s worth noting Lincoln Riley is 1-6 against AP top 10 teams since becoming USC’s head coach and the Trojans have been outscored 257-204.

articles.title: Fantasy Baseball Offseason Tracker: Kevin Gausman gets prove-it deal from Tigers; Alec Bohm goes to Royals
articles.summary: Meanwhile, the Orioles have swapped out one free agent pitcher (Trevor Rogers) for another (Freddy Peralta)
body: A lockout may be coming, but nobody told the hot stove. It's already burning bright with even the biggest prize, two-time Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal, coming off the market. Trevor Rogers and Freddy Peralta soon followed, and at this rate, most of the marquee free agents will be nailed down by Thanksgiving.

There's a reason for the urgency. Once the lockout becomes official, the signings -- and all other transactions -- will cease, but those that occur before then will still count toward the date when baseball is allowed to resume. So we'd better document them all here, just like any other offseason, breaking down their impact for Fantasy Baseball.

That's what Scott White and Chris Towers intend to do over the next few weeks, at least, before everything goes quiet. They'll eventually pick up where they left off when the hot stove heats up again in... March? Hopefully not much later than that.
Whatever the timeline, you'll want this page bookmarked so you can get the first word on everything that happens.
